result.summary: Validates timeout arguments in the mining interface methods waitNext and waitTipChanged, throwing a std::runtime_error if the timeout is negative or NaN. Updates documentation in interfaces/mining.h and adds functional test coverage verifying remote exceptions over Cap'n Proto IPC.
result.problem: IPC callers can supply negative or NaN timeouts to the mining interface. In debug builds, passing negative or NaN values triggers an Assume failure that aborts the node; in release builds, NaN values can bypass comparison clamps and pass invalid deadlines to wait primitives.
evidence: Author reproduction: 'On debug builds, a negative or NaN timeout fails this check and aborts the node. I reproduced this with a timeout of -1.0.'

Author note on severity: 'I'm not aware of any client that sends these values (sv2-tp, for example, requires an interval of at least one second), so this is hardening against bad input from ipc clients.'
result.changed_since_previous: Switched from clamping negative and NaN timeouts to zero to throwing a std::runtime_error that propagates as an IPC exception (the PR description text still mentions clamping to zero, but the diff and commit message reflect the exception).
result.card: Throws a runtime exception for negative or NaN timeout parameters in mining interface methods waitNext and waitTipChanged over IPC. IPC clients passing negative or NaN values previously triggered an Assume failure that aborted debug builds, and could cause unintended wait timing on release builds. The author reproduced the debug crash with a timeout of -1.0, though noted no known IPC clients currently send invalid timeouts.

risk.why: Mistakes would be restricted to IPC mining callers rejecting otherwise valid wait timeouts.
